name: Milky Way galaxy
headline: diameter
description: The Milky Way is the spiral galaxy that contains our solar system, with an estimated 100 to 400 billion stars. NASA describes its disc of stars as about 100,000 light-years across, while a 2018 study led by the Instituto de Astrofisica de Canarias found disc stars far enough out to suggest a diameter of around 200,000 light-years. The solar system lies about halfway out from the centre and takes about 240 million years to complete one orbit.

measures.label: Disc diameter (estimated)
measures.note: Estimated diameter of the stellar disc: about 100,000 ly (NASA) to around 200,000 ly (IAC 2018 study)

facts.text: NASA describes the Milky Way as a spiral galaxy with a disc of stars spanning more than 100,000 light-years; our solar system takes about 240 million years to orbit its centre.
NASA estimates the galaxy probably contains 100 to 400 billion stars.
Measurements with Hubble and Gaia put the Milky Way's total mass at about 1.5 trillion solar masses, including a supermassive black hole of about 4 million solar masses.
A 2018 IAC-led study using APOGEE and LAMOST survey data found disc stars out to more than three times the Sun's distance from the galactic centre, implying a disc around 200,000 light-years across.

caveats: All sizes are estimated. A galaxy's disc has no sharp edge, so its diameter depends on which stars are counted; the much larger dark-matter halo is not included.
The mass (about 1.5 trillion solar masses) is given only in solar masses, which the site's units do not support, so it appears as a fact rather than a measure.
